Final Technical Report 20/57 4 STRUCTURAL DESIGN The structure design has been completed reevaluating the hull, completing the structure with several additional required elements and integrating the jack up towers. Finally, the stability reevaluation of the completed structure was accomplished. A summary of the conclusions is described below: 4.1 Hull design Firstly, the scantling of the MTV has been developed during the PDR phase following the applicable ABS standards. The obtained midship section drawing was submitted to ABS returning comments to IDOM, which were implemented in the drawings. As some of the loading conditions are not covered by common ships rules and standards, the whole hull has been also validated by means of FEM. The global stress analysis shows satisfactory results. The overall Von Mises stress level is below allowable 2 stress of 150N/mm . A general view of the final scantling can be seen in the following figure. Figure 4-1 Hull design, internal stiffeners overview There were 2 structural areas within the hull which have been modified during the final design phase, the platforms and the CEC supporting structure foundations. Their designs are out of scope of common ships rules and standards. Thus, the validation has been performed by means of FEM. The platform deflection showed values up to 45 mm under jack up configuration with PDR, which were excessive form structural point of view. The modification accomplished in the platforms (see Figure 4-1) increasing the height and therefore, the inertia, shows a deflection reduction from 45mm to 5mm. This modification leads to a negligible increase in the vessel overall weight. 4.2 Additional Elements Besides, some elements within FDR phase have been included and analyzed completing the structure: the deck fittings on the deck , the anchor support (see Figure 4-2) and the heavy lifting pad eyes. Standardized elements under catalogue have been selected to the extent possible. If this was not possible, the developed design has been validated by means of FEM. The accommodation of these elements leads to modify the adjacent areas of the deck or hull to withstand the loads. Final Technical Report 21/57 Figure 4-2 Anchor support design The structure has been completed for this FDR with the design integration of the jack up towers. The design was developed by a potential supplier (EBI) based on the loads obtained from a global analyses of the jack up system accomplished by IDOM. Final Technical Report 22/57 5 STABILITY ANALYSIS This section provides a summary of the stability assessment of the MTV. The stability of a vessel is a crucial aspect of its overall safety and performance, and this section aims to evaluate the vessel’s compliance with relevant international regulations and standards. The section includes an analysis of the vessel’s stability characteristics, such as its metacentric height and righting arm, and an assessment of its stability in different loading conditions. After verifying the necessary stability criteria, IMO codes were followed for the assessment.
